text.p: Sampdoria, reduced to 10 men, scored two goals late in the second half to come back and beat champions A.C.Milan 3-2 on Sunday and move to within two points of Juventus at the top of Italy's Serie A.
European champions Juventus, held 0-0 at Cagliari, now have 37 points from 19 matches followed by Sampdoria and Bologna, who moved into third place on 31 points after steamrollering lowly Verona 6-1.

Milan, with goals by Liberia's George Weah either side of the interval, appeared to be on their way to a key home victory after second-placed Sampdoria's goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron was sent off in the 22nd minute for fouling Weah.

But just as Milan seemed certain winners, Yugoslavian defender Sinisa Mihajlovic blasted home a free kick to equalise in the 74th minute and, five minutes later, winger Marco Carparelli added the shock winner.
Veteran captain Roberto Mancini had put the Genoa side ahead in the first minute.
The sight of Italian captain Paolo Maldini hobbling off during the first half also raised questions about his fitness for the World Cup qualifier against England at Wembley on February 12.
Elsewhere, Enrico Chiesa's late goal gave Parma a 1-0 win over Piacenza to move into a three-way tie for fourth place with Inter, held 0-0 at Perugia, and Vicenza, beaten 2-0 at Roma.
